screening_decisions.reason: Although this is an RCT comparing clomipramine with placebo in depressed adolescents (mean age 16.2 years), the intervention was administered intravenously (200 mg iv), not orally. The selection criteria explicitly require orally administered tricyclic drugs.
This RCT compares fluoxetine (an SSRI, not a tricyclic antidepressant) with placebo. The review is specifically about tricyclic drugs.

This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of orally administered nortriptyline (a tricyclic antidepressant) in depressed adolescents aged 12-17 years with major depressive disorder. It meets all selection criteria.
This is a qualitative review article, not a randomized controlled trial. It does not compare a tricyclic drug with placebo.

This is a double-blind pilot study (RCT) comparing oral imipramine (a tricyclic antidepressant) with placebo in depressed children. It meets the population (depressed children), intervention (oral tricyclic), comparison (placebo), and design (RCT) criteria.

This is a randomized, double-blind crossover trial comparing oral amitriptyline (a tricyclic antidepressant, 1-2.5 mg/kg/day) with placebo in children aged 9-12 years with major depressive disorder. It meets all selection criteria.
This is a Cochrane review focusing on newer generation antidepressants (particularly SSRIs), not tricyclic drugs. It is a systematic review, not a primary RCT.

While this RCT compares imipramine with placebo, the study population was selected based on school refusal (not depression as the primary condition), and the primary outcome was school attendance. Although participants had comorbid major depression, the study is focused on treating school refusal rather than depression per se.

This is a double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT investigating oral imipramine (up to 5 mg/kg/day) in prepubertal children with major depressive disorder. It includes a five-week double-blind placebo-controlled design and meets all selection criteria.

This is a three-arm RCT (paroxetine, imipramine, placebo) in adolescents with major depression. It includes a direct comparison of oral imipramine (a tricyclic antidepressant) versus placebo in depressed adolescents aged approximately 12-18 years, thereby meeting the review's selection criteria for the tricyclic versus placebo comparison.

This is a review article discussing the pharmacological mechanisms of antidepressants. It is not a randomized controlled trial comparing tricyclic drugs with placebo for depression in children or adolescents.

This study examines SSRI safety in overdose using case reports and poison control data. It is not an RCT, does not involve tricyclic drugs as the intervention of interest, and does not assess efficacy for depression.
This is a methodological paper about meta-analysis statistics. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial of tricyclic drugs for depression in children or adolescents.
This is a case series/review of children with amitriptyline poisoning. It is not an RCT and does not assess the efficacy of tricyclic drugs for depression.

This appears to be a secondary analysis examining how comorbid disorders predict treatment response, rather than a primary report of an RCT comparing tricyclic drugs with placebo. The abstract does not establish that this is the primary trial report meeting all selection criteria.

This is a randomized, placebo-controlled trial of oral desipramine (a tricyclic antidepressant) versus placebo in adolescents aged 13-18 years with major depressive disorder. It meets all selection criteria.
This is a narrative review and opinion paper about the state of psychopharmacology research. It is not a randomized controlled trial comparing tricyclic drugs with placebo.

This RCT compares alprazolam and imipramine with placebo for school refusal, not for depression as the primary condition. The population is defined by school refusal rather than by depression, and the primary focus is on anxiety and school attendance outcomes rather than depression.
This is a case series/review of poison control data on accidental tricyclic antidepressant ingestions in young children. It is not an RCT and does not assess efficacy for depression.

This is a randomized, double-blind, parallel-design, placebo-controlled trial of oral amitriptyline (5 mg/kg/day) in adolescents aged 12-17 years with major depressive disorder. It meets all selection criteria.

This double-blind trial investigates clomipramine for school phobia/school refusal, not for depression as the primary condition. Although depression symptoms are mentioned, the study population is defined by school phobia/neurotic disorder, not by depression.

This is a meta-analysis of phase II studies comparing paroxetine with amitriptyline in hospitalized depressed adults aged 18-65 years. It is not a primary RCT, the population is adults, and it does not include a placebo comparison relevant to the review criteria.

This study examined plasma imipramine levels and response in 20 prepubertal children with major depression. However, there is no mention of randomization or a placebo control group; all children appear to have received imipramine after a psychotherapy run-in. It does not meet the RCT or placebo comparison criteria.
This is a 10-week randomized, controlled trial comparing oral amitriptyline (a tricyclic antidepressant) with placebo in adolescents with major depressive disorder. It meets all selection criteria.

This is a secondary analysis of a double-blind RCT focusing on medication compliance, side effects, and guessing of drug assignment. It is not the primary efficacy report of the underlying trial, and the underlying trial population (anxious-depressed adolescents with school refusal) was selected for school refusal rather than depression as the primary condition.
